title: Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic)
capsule: The Napoleonic Kingdom of Naples was a French client monarchy in southern Italy established in February 1806 after Napoleon Bonaparte declared the Bourbon Ferdinando IV deposed for allying with the Third Coalition. Joseph Bonaparte ruled 1806–1808, abolishing feudalism and reorganizing the kingdom into thirteen provinces on French prefectural lines, before being transferred to the Spanish throne; Joachim Murat, Napoleon's brother-in-law, then reigned 1808–1815 and pursued ambitious, if erratic, attempts to win Italian national sentiment. Murat's defeat at the Battle of Tolentino on 3 May 1815 ended his reign; the Congress of Vienna restored Ferdinand, who merged Naples and Sicily into the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1816.
